nodes.description: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in TUBGCP6 remove or reduce a component of the gamma-tubulin ring complex, the machine that nucleates microtubules from the centrosome. The mechanism is the same class as TUBGCP4-related MCCRP3: insufficient nucleating capacity rather than a defective tubulin subunit. Reported alleles include compound heterozygous deletions, which makes the loss-of-function nature explicit rather than inferred.

genetic_context.description: Biallelic loss-of-function alleles, described as such by the primary literature, and including compound heterozygous deletions. This contrasts with the dominant missense mechanisms of the tubulin isotype genes and matches the recessive loss-of-function pattern of the other gamma-tubulin-complex disorder, TUBGCP4-related MCCRP3.

nodes.description: The developmental endpoint. Brain growth is reduced to the point of microcephaly recognizable prenatally, and the retina and choroid develop abnormally, with visual impairment evident during the first year of life. Dysmorphic features accompany both. The timing is informative: a prenatally detectable microcephaly and a first-year visual deficit place the critical period in fetal development rather than in postnatal maintenance.
